text:
customer-jordan: Hi team — we had a traffic surge around 11:15 PST and our calls to /v1/rerank started returning 502/504. p95 latency spiked from ~120ms to 3.2s, lots of retries. Not sure if payload size or concurrency. Can someone look?

alex: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste a sample request (headers + body) and any request_id you saw in responses? Also how many concurrent requests were you running?

customer-jordan: Sample payload below (simplified):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "query": "best hotels in seattle",
  "candidates": ["doc1","doc2", ..., "doc20"],
  "top_k": 5
}
```
We were sending ~200 concurrent requests from a single region, bursty for ~6 minutes. Response headers had `x-request-id: rq_9f3a` and HTTP 504 a few times.

sre-jen: Seeing matching traces — gateway returned 504 upstream timeout. Nginx logs show `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream` from model-worker-2. Also intermittent `connection reset by peer`. Paste log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:15:12Z] gateway nginx: 10.0.5.12 - - "POST /v1/rerank" 504 0 "-" "-" upstream: "http://10.0.7.22:8080/rerank" host: "api.redwood.ai"
[2026-03-15T18:15:13Z] model-worker-2 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) total-vm: 1.2G, anon-rss: 980M
```

oncall-eric: That OOM on worker aligns with heavy batch sizes + concurrency. The runtime sometimes holds KV cache + big candidate tensors per request. If too many in flight it swaps.

maya: Short term mitigation: 1) ask clients to reduce parallelism (client-side backoff + lower concurrency) 2) enable per-tenant concurrency cap in gateway (we can set to 50 requests) 3) roll out a temporary fallback to a smaller rerank model variant (fewer params) for the affected customer.

alex: Customer, can you throttle to 50 concurrent requests and retry the 6-minute window? If errors stop, we'll push gateway limits. Also we'll collect traces for `rq_9f3a` and similar ids.

customer-jordan: Throttling to 50 brought errors down immediately. Thanks. But we need a more permanent fix — campaign traffic will repeat.

sre-jen: Action items:
- Collect full traces and per-request memory usage for the time window (I have a script running).
- Add temporary per-tenant concurrency cap and return 429 instead of letting requests pile up.
- Reduce allowed candidate batch size from 50 -> 20 for rerank API (PR in flight).

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1173 (rerank high qps 5xx) assigned to oncall-eric and sre-jen :rotating_light:

oncall-eric: I'll coordinate a quick deploy: set tenant concurrency=50, enforce candidate_limit=20, and enable fallback model alias `rerank-small` for the account. That should cut memory pressure. Will also add a gate that rejects requests with `top_k>10` for now.

maya: For longer term: autoscaler tuning — increase headroom for model-worker group and add an eviction-safe memory limit to avoid OOM kills. Also fix gateway retry logic: prefer exponential backoff with jitter and limit total retry attempts to 2 to avoid thundering herd.

alex: I've asked product to notify the customer about the temporary limits and the planned timeline. Also opening a postmortem doc (link to be added).

customer-jordan: Appreciate the quick triage. Two questions: 1) Any recommendation on client-side retries/backoff? 2) Will billing be affected if we get many 429s?

maya: 1) Use exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max 2s, cap retries at 2. Prefer idempotent narrow retries for rerank. 2) 429s are not billable — we'll coordinate credits if our rate limiting was the root cause.

sre-jen: Repro steps for infra team (as requested):
- Run load test: 200 concurrent clients issuing rerank with 20 candidates and top_k=5 for 5 minutes.
- Monitor worker memory, nginx upstream_latencies, gateway queue length.
- Validate that with candidate_limit=20 / concurrency=50 errors drop.

alex: I'll keep this thread updated with trace links and the postmortem. Next update in ~2 hours after the deploy. :thumbsup:

oncall-eric: Deploy done to prod (concurrency cap + candidate_limit + fallback). Early telemetry looks good: p95 down to 180ms and 5xxs near zero for the affected tenant. Leaving incident open for monitoring.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1173 updated: severity=high -> monitoring, next update in 30m.

alex: Closing note for follow-up items: 1) postmortem w/ root cause (OOM + insufficient gateway backoff), 2) long-term autoscaler + memory accounting, 3) SDK guidance on client-side concurrency and retry defaults.

customer-jordan: Thanks everyone — will validate on our side and report any anomalies.

sre-jen: Adding one more note: keep an eye for `connection reset by peer` patterns even after fixes — could indicate kernel-level OOM throttling or transient network flaps. If that persists we'll dig into worker container memory cgroups and host swap activity.
